title: Drakengard
synopsis: The first point in the Drakengard and Nier lineage, retained as a playable reference copy and as evidence of where that history began.

catalog.mediumForm: Pressed optical disc · PlayStation 2 retail edition

custody.physical: Complete in box: case, pressed disc, manual, and original cover insert
custody.condition: Complete in box. Light shelf wear consistent with age. Preserved as a playable reference copy.

curatorNotes:
I spent years thinking of Drakengard as a game I would own eventually. It was never entirely out of reach; it was simply passed over whenever another work felt more urgent. Copies were uncommon in the places I looked, and the search remained open.

What changed was the purpose of the shelf. The aim was no longer to own everything, but to keep a smaller group of works whose histories deserved attention. Drakengard belongs here because so much followed from it. Nier inherited ideas, images, and unease that Yoko Taro and Cavia first committed to this game.

It is a difficult work in every sense: mechanically uneven, severe in tone, and often uncomfortable. Those qualities are part of the record. This copy is preserved not as an endorsement or a score, but as the beginning of a lineage that became more important with time.
collectionNotes:
Acquired in June 2026 while completing the Drakengard 1–3 shelf. The North American PlayStation 2 edition is retained as the reference copy for this filing.

The acquisition marked a change in collecting practice: away from accumulation and toward deliberate custody. Drakengard was among the works that clarified that distinction. The copy remains complete in box and is kept with its original manual and cover insert.

The acquisition photograph records the three principal Drakengard releases together at the moment the lineage was completed.

preservation.playableOn: Sony PlayStation 2; compatible North American PlayStation hardware
preservation.compatibility: Pressed for North American PlayStation 2 consoles. The retained disc remains the primary access copy.
preservation.concerns: Optical-disc aging and surface damage remain the principal risks. The disc is stored upright in its original case under stable, dry conditions; printed materials remain housed with the copy.
preservation.knownRevisions: First issued in Japan as Drag-on Dragoon in 2003. The North American localization followed in 2004 under the title Drakengard.
preservation.availability: The original physical edition is out of print and circulates through the secondary market. No current digital edition replaces this reference copy.
